root_causes.finding: V42.25 moved TypeScript repair candidates outside the accepted workspace and excluded node_modules, while V42.24 invoked the accepted workspace's tsc against that external clone. Node resolution could no longer reach installed React/Vite dependencies, so correct repairs appeared to regress from 8 diagnostics to 57-64 diagnostics and were rejected.
V42.30's last-mile regression asserted transformed source text but did not compile a real external dependency-less candidate, so it did not cover the failing integration boundary.
After the TypeScript tail closed, the real Vite build exposed a package alias mapping @tauri-apps/api to a missing local JSON path. The alias hijacked legitimate package subpath imports.

The Node validator treated a non-noop test script as mandatory, but resume/test-debt policy allowed all test files to be absent. Vitest therefore failed every otherwise-green project with 'No test files found'.
Accepted compiler repairs did not invalidate the matching current_blocker in the compact event projection, so later resume logic could continue targeting an already-repaired file.

The supplied Jarvis source identified V42.30 while the supplied checkpoint projection contained later V42.32-V42.34 metadata. A stale running process or mismatched code/checkpoint lineage can make reported behavior differ from the files being inspected. V42.35 adds a disk/running-engine guard.

acceptance_scope: The exact reported frontend/compiler failure path is reproduced and repaired. V42.35 preserves the universal adapter/declared-command architecture and existing-project edit mode. No finite regression can guarantee every future prompt, language, SDK, operating system, or external service; Jarvis must continue to report host-limited validation honestly instead of claiming completion without the required native toolchain.
